A1.justification: Both complete 19-page PDFs describe the same self-certainty and Borda-voting research. Text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original accuracy experiments on mathematical reasoning, code reasoning, and code generation in Tables 1-3 and Figure 8, with further experiments and analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 reports the same original benchmark evaluations in Tables 1-3 and Figure 8, alongside the supplementary empirical results in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Sections 3-4 retain the same KL-based self-certainty metric, token-level averaging, and rank-based Borda voting rule. No method component or selection procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use LiveBench-Math, GSM8K, MATH, CRUXEval-O, and LiveCodeBench. The represented tasks, MATH difficulty-level evaluations, and cross-dataset analyses in Appendix B are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator participation is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including greedy decoding, FirstAns, perplexity, USC, self-consistency, the PRM/ORM comparisons in Table 1, and alternative voting comparisons in Tables 2, 5, and 6.

E3.justification: Section 5 retains the same models, splits, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.9, 64-response sampling pool, candidate subset sizes, answer masking, and USC fallback procedure. Appendix experimental settings also match.

E4.justification: The correctness and response-length analyses, Borda-parameter sensitivity study, difficulty breakdowns, empirical-versus-uniform distribution ablation, and Appendix C case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Five-repetition averaging in Section 5.1 and the specified single-trial evaluations in Section 5.2 and Appendix B remain unchanged. No seed information or uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1-6, Figures 1-12, and the case studies retain identical results. For example, Table 1 reports MATH accuracy at N=64 of 56.70 for self-certainty and 64.10 for Borda with p=1.2 in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)-(11) are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same derivation, Theorem A.1, Corollary A.2, proof, and qualifications; Equation (10) only moves to the next page.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1 contribution bullets, and Section 8 retain the same claims about scalable reward-free selection, improved reasoning through Borda voting, and applicability to open-ended generation.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning error propagation, length robustness, Borda weighting, generalization, and underperformance against self-consistency on definitive-answer tasks are unchanged. Section 7 and the appendix discussions retain the same qualifications and future directions.

D1.justification: Both provide the same code link, ZeroEval framework, NVIDIA A100 hardware information, sampling parameters, tuning advice, and Appendix C prompts. No technical or resource-access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the full reference list contain the same works and research positioning. References crossing different page boundaries in v3 are retained, rather than added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 identifies Xuandong Zhao as corresponding author through a dagger and added footnote, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Minor reflow changes page breaks and some display positions, including moving Equation (10) from page 4 to page 5. Figure and table designs, captions, and contents are unchanged; appendix pages 13-19 are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v3 adds a corresponding-author designation and minor layout reflow while preserving the scientific text, methods, theory, results, and reproducibility information, including all appendices. The administrative clarification does not materially improve or diminish the paper's overall quality.
